exercise.name: Barbell Palms Up Wrist Curl over a bench
aliases: Barbell wrist curl over a bench
Bench barbell wrist curl, palms up

reference.title: Barbell Palms Up Wrist Curl over a bench
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be read from this environment, gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the hands curl up, in as they lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, 0.4 s squeeze, 1.7 s down

prescription.tempo: 1 s up, short squeeze, 1.5-2 s down
prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: light; a full, pain-free range matters more than load.

cues.text: Kneel behind a flat bench, forearms across the pad, palms up, wrists just past the far edge; underhand grip about shoulder width.
Curl the hands up from the wrists; the forearms stay flat on the pad.
Squeeze the forearms at the top.
Lower the bar slowly until the wrists are bent back.
Keep the forearms on the pad and repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the forearms off the bench
mistakes.fix: Keep the forearms pinned to the pad; only the hands move.
Slide forward until the wrists are just past the edge so the hands move freely.

kinematics.norm: Healthy adults used up to about 54 degrees of wrist flexion and 60 degrees of extension in daily tasks, functional range about 40 each way (Ryu 1991); a curl goes a little further, to a comfortable end range without pain (clinical opinion)
Forearms rest across the pad and stay still; the wrists just past the edge so the hands move freely (clinical opinion)
Slow and controlled, about 1 s up, a short squeeze and 1.5-2 s down (clinical opinion); wrist resistance programmes used 1-4 sets of about 15 reps (J Hand Ther 2012)

cautions: Use a light bar and a pad or mat under the knees.
Wrist pain or a recent wrist injury: shorten the range or skip.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knees: sit on the end of the bench and rest the forearms on the thighs instead.
regressions: Dumbbell wrist curl, one arm at a time.
